races.name: Get Best Odds With Oddschecker Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Louis The Fifth
runners_data.comment: A No Nay Never colt bought for 215,000 euros at the breeze-ups and half-brother to a very useful 5-6f performer — Louis The Fifth has the pedigree credentials to make a bold debut showing; dam was a smart juvenile at 8f. Worth taking seriously on breeding alone.

runners_data.name: Sod Hall Lane
runners_data.comment: A Blue Point colt out of a useful 7f dam — Sod Hall Lane makes his debut here and our figures rank him last of five. Unless market support is strong, little to recommend him above better-bred rivals on this occasion.

runners_data.name: By Jove Grace
runners_data.comment: An Inns Of Court filly bought for £70,000 at the breeze-ups — By Jove Grace has an able dam at 6f and makes her first start here. Connections are experienced but she is probably one to monitor rather than back on debut unless the market suggests otherwise.

runners_data.name: In The Black
runners_data.comment: Closely related to a high-class 6f performer and out of a very useful 5f dam — In The Black is a 320,000gns Havana Grey filly with strong physical appeal and top breeding for a 2yo contest; holds genuine appeal for a first start. The main risk is the unknown of a first racecourse start.

runners_data.name: Queen Of Christmas
runners_data.comment: Experience counts from a debut fifth — Queen Of Christmas came behind a subsequent Group-race candidate at Nottingham and now steps into what looks a gentler opportunity; the stable excels with its youngsters at this venue and she arrives with a debut experience to call on. Should take a clear forward step second time out.

races.name: Bet Smarter With Oddschecker+ EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Enhancing
runners_data.comment: Shaped with encouragement on debut at Newbury — not disgraced over today's distance on good to firm going — and now gets a tongue-tie for the first time to help Enhancing settle. Good connections and scope for improvement suggest a more forward display is on the cards.

runners_data.name: Independent Roze
runners_data.comment: A Bangkok filly out of a useful 5f dam and half-sister to a moderate performer at 6f — Independent Roze is on debut here with modest pedigree angles and our figures rank her last. Hard to be bullish here unless the market provides a positive steer.

runners_data.name: Love Tanya
runners_data.comment: A well-bred Blue Point filly bought for 110,000 euros — Love Tanya is half-sister to a smart stayer and from connections capable of producing a forward debut performance. Worth a look on breeding and connections alone.

runners_data.name: One Shot Kodi
runners_data.comment: Beaten 10 lengths on debut at Redcar, One Shot Kodi needs a major step forward to figure here; our figures rank her fifth of six and the debut run gives little encouragement that she has the class for this level.

runners_data.name: Ruby Moon
runners_data.comment: A No Nay Never filly half-sister to a useful 7f performer — Ruby Moon arrives on debut with a fair family profile but our figures rank her fourth, and the pedigree suggests she faces a stiff ask on debut without a clear market move.

runners_data.name: Silesia
runners_data.comment: Three outings without a win but placed on every start, Silesia is appearing to need the step to 6f to show her best — she found the pace of the front pair too hot last time at Beverley over five furlongs. Acts on good to soft and good, and looks the most solid prospect in this field.

races.name: Download The Oddschecker App EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Social Spirit
runners_data.comment: Posted two starts showing progression, including a solid effort at Epsom in a stronger 2yo heat, and the step up to 7f here is an angle that could help Social Spirit — versatile from 5-6f on good to soft and good to firm. Should be competitive, though up against respected debutants.

runners_data.name: Telegraphic
runners_data.comment: A Kameko colt half-brother to a very useful 6f performer out of a moderate dam — Telegraphic makes his debut with an interesting sibling profile and is one to treat with respect; the market will reveal how confident connections are going in.

runners_data.name: The First Drop
runners_data.comment: A Lope Y Fernandez colt out of a moderate dam — The First Drop makes his debut here and connections have shown they can have a juvenile primed first time; one to watch in the market before writing off.

runners_data.name: King Of Persia
runners_data.comment: Unable to land a blow on debut here at Carlisle — beaten six-and-a-half lengths in a maiden — King Of Persia is trained by a top course handler and improvement is expected from that first outing; our figures rank him fifth and he should move forward.

runners_data.name: Mia Fantasia
runners_data.comment: A 40,000 euros Make Believe colt out of a dam who showed fair ability at 8f and half-brother to a useful mare — Mia Fantasia debuts for strong connections who are more than capable of having a juvenile ready first time. Worth watching the market before dismissing.

runners_data.name: Parry Green
runners_data.comment: A Massaat gelding out of a moderate dam, with a half-brother who showed fair form at 7f — Parry Green makes his debut here and our figures rank him last of eleven. Hard to fancy unless betting points the other way.

runners_data.name: Platinum Force
runners_data.comment: A 50,000 euros Blackbeard half-brother to a useful 6f performer — Platinum Force is bred to run well as a juvenile and debuts for connections with a strong record preparing youngsters; deserves plenty of respect on his first outing.

runners_data.name: Ricky Punting
runners_data.comment: Below par at Pontefract last time when held in first-time cheekpieces — finding little and well beaten after being off the pace — Ricky Punting now steps up to 7f, which suits, and tries the gear again. A clear rebound is required; prior form showed enough to suggest improvement is possible.

runners_data.name: Be More Ruthless
runners_data.comment: A Rajasinghe filly out of a smart 5f dam and half-sister to a useful stayer — Be More Ruthless debuts with a handler in good shape but the breeding suggests this is a tough first assignment; our figures rank her ninth of eleven.

runners_data.name: Mrs Mole
runners_data.comment: Shaped with encouragement on her debut fourth at Leicester — not far behind in a 7f maiden — Mrs Mole is effective at 7f on good ground and should go forward from that first start; the form looks solid and improvement is likely as the season develops.

runners_data.name: Wells Fargo Stage
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on her debut at Redcar — a major step forward is required — Wells Fargo Stage arrives here with a trainer who has an excellent record at this venue. Our figures rank her tenth, and without market signals it is hard to be optimistic about her prospects.

races.name: Lady Dacre Bell Handicap

runners_data.name: Marry The Night
runners_data.note: Easterby's consistent performer has shown strong recent form (three wins in last six) and wears hood headgear; a natural up-with-pace racer who will find prominent positions contested in this field, meaning she may have to work harder than ideal for her spot.
runners_data.comment: Thriving through the spring with back-to-back wins before a well-beaten turf run at Carlisle last time, Marry The Night's sharper form has clearly come on the AW — first-time cheekpieces the hope of reversing that latest effort here. Effective over 8f on any ground but most comfortable off turf.

runners_data.name: I Can Dance
runners_data.note: Returning after a 273-day absence for Charlie Johnston, so fitness is the critical question; showed promise at Haydock and Goodwood earlier in the year and the step up to a mile on good ground suits, but the layoff is a significant risk factor.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed as a juvenile before a promising third last time — I Can Dance is a well-bred type returning from 273 days off and arrives with upside; effective at 7-8f. The lengthy layoff is the obvious concern going into her first handicap start.

runners_data.name: Pension Pot
runners_data.note: Barron's hold-up performer is back quickly (12 days) and has decent course-distance form on similar going; tends to need things to fall right from the rear and the race shape here may not generate the pace surge she needs late on.
runners_data.comment: Third at Chester last time off today's mark, Pension Pot finished with purpose after a sluggish early display and stays a mile on soft, good and the AW; yet to win in her last five starts. Our figures rank her ninth of eleven — needs significant improvement to reach the front end here.

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Easterby who races from behind and has a strong record placing on Good going (four placed from 15 similar-ground runs); D Allan takes the ride and if the prominent horses tire late he could be strongest of the closers.
runners_data.comment: Unlucky not to finish closer than a length third at Ripon last time — clear improvement on the runs prior — Barley goes in first-time cheekpieces with a top yard in her corner; effective over 8f on soft and good to firm. Yet to win in recent starts but the trajectory is heading upward.

runners_data.name: Harswell Ruby
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's mare won at this trip on Good last season and has five runs on similar ground returning a solid 10 placings from 15; Joanna Mason partners a horse that genuinely wants this prominent position and the track and conditions suit well.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time at a mark just 1lb higher than today's, Harswell Ruby showed she is running to her level and handles today's distance and going. Ranked seventh of eleven here, she is on a competitive mark but needs things to fall her way to take a hand.

runners_data.name: Runswick
runners_data.note: Dunlop's three-year-old is the confirmed lone front-runner and Tudhope is an astute pilot for a lead-and-try mission; lightly raced at Carlisle's mile, though form on soft ground is more plentiful than on quick, which is worth monitoring on this Good to Firm surface.
runners_data.comment: Two solid placed finishes since returning, Runswick was denied by the narrowest of margins at Chester last time off a 2lb lower mark — stays a mile and acts on soft and good. Our top-rated horse in the field by a clear margin, the 2lb rise may not be enough to deny him.

runners_data.name: Aqua Bear
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' three-year-old won at 7f at Nottingham and was placed at Hamilton on similar ground; a genuine prominent type who should secure a position just off Runswick's pace, and the step up from 7f to a flat mile looks straightforward.
runners_data.comment: Good prior form before Goodwood but Aqua Bear failed to see out the trip when well beaten there most recently, and a clear rebound is required; handles 6-7f on a range of surfaces. Ranked eighth here and the first run back is worth treating with some caution.

runners_data.name: Wetsand
runners_data.note: James Owen's hold-up juvenile has modest form figures but two wins in the form string suggest ability when conditions click; the Good going is fine but this runner needs plenty to go right from the back and the race shape is not obviously ideal.
runners_data.comment: Outpaced and always in arrear in her last several starts — unable to demonstrate any progress on her earlier efforts — Wetsand is effective at 7-8f on a sound surface. The question is whether she can produce what her earlier form hinted at.

runners_data.name: Popeye Doyle
runners_data.note: Bedi's runner wears a tongue-tie and is a genuine hold-up horse with a placed run on Good at a mile; redistributed into midfield on the map because there is no room at the back in this field configuration, meaning his race depends on finding that position naturally under Shay Farmer.
runners_data.comment: First-time tongue-boot and blinkers and yet to win in her last five starts — Popeye Doyle ran to her level at Wetherby last time over today's trip on a sound surface; capable of a decent effort but inconsistent. Our figures rank her second-bottom here and a bold showing would surprise.

runners_data.name: Geo
runners_data.note: Goldie's four-year-old has excellent course-and-distance form (2 wins and 3 places from 13 runs on Good going at the mile) and Tom Marquand is a high-class booking; a true hold-up type who is mapped to midfield due to field congestion at the rear, and his record on this surface is the standout statistic in the race.
runners_data.comment: Close second at Carlisle last time off today's mark — moving up through the gears to near-miss form — and a notable jockey engagement adds to the appeal for Geo; acts at 7-8f on a sound surface. Ranked sixth here but the trajectory is clearly improving.

runners_data.name: Pepsea
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's three-year-old ran yesterday (1 day ago) which is an immediate flag; four consecutive fourth-place finishes suggest a consistent but limited performer, and the very quick turnaround will need a convincing explanation before this runner can be taken seriously.
runners_data.comment: All four starts showing a pattern of close finishes without quite getting there — Pepsea ran to her level at Carlisle yesterday, just fading in the closing stages of a novice at this track; the yard in good shape and the switch to handicap company on today's going opens another door. Well worth a look on her first start from a handicap mark.

races.paceDynamic: Runswick is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival for the lead, should stride into a comfortable, uncontested position from the outset on Good to Firm ground at Carlisle's flat mile. The pace will be sustainable rather than scorching — a single leader dictating through the early exchanges without being pressured creates a relatively even gallop, which historically at this track rewards horses that can travel prominently and produce a sustained effort in the straight. Harswell Ruby and Aqua Bear are the natural challengers to sit just off Runswick's shoulder, while Marry The Night is a genuine prominent type who will be squeezed for that position given the volume of horses wanting to race forward. The field holds more prominent/front-running types than the map can accommodate cleanly — Marry The Night, Popeye Doyle, and Geo are redistributed from their natural roles, meaning the early order may be more scrappy than the lone-leader headline suggests. This race shape — a single honest pace-setter with a small pocket of prominent horses just behind — most strongly favours hold-up horses able to settle and finish powerfully, provided they avoid traffic; but the premium position of Runswick and the genuine prominent types immediately behind it means those racing in the first three or four are best placed tactically.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Runswick controls, prominent strike
scenarios.trigger: If Runswick leads uncontested and sets an honest but not punishing pace, allowing the closest pursuers to land in ideal position.
scenarios.body: If Runswick leads uncontested and sets an honest but not punishing pace, allowing the closest pursuers to land in ideal position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late surge beats tired leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than expected and front-runners flatten out in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace is fractionally stronger than expected and front-runners flatten out in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Crowded early, pace collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the jostling among the displaced prominent types creates a messy opening and the field funnels into a slow early crawl.
scenarios.body: If the jostling among the displaced prominent types creates a messy opening and the field funnels into a slow early crawl.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-up finisher swamps field
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine hold-up horses find a clear run early in the straight and the prominent horses have all raced too freely.
scenarios.body: If the genuine hold-up horses find a clear run early in the straight and the prominent horses have all raced too freely.

watchPoints.text: Pepsea ran just one day ago — watch for any withdrawn/declaration issue and monitor market moves closely, as a horse running 24 hours after its last start on Good to Firm ground is a significant welfare and performance concern.

Geo's course-and-distance record (2 wins, 3 places from 13 similar-going runs) is the strongest statistical profile in the field — if Tom Marquand finds a clear run from midfield in the straight, this horse is live to pounce at a potentially big price.

The cluster of prominent types — Marry The Night, Harswell Ruby, Aqua Bear — battling for the two or three positions directly behind Runswick could cause significant early crowding; watch for any jostling on the first bend that shuffles a fancied runner back into traffic.

Runswick's form is predominantly on Soft ground (3 of 5 recent runs) and the going is Good to Firm — watch whether Tudhope seeks to conserve energy early or pushes on, as any sign of the horse struggling for footing could completely reshape the pace picture.

I Can Dance returns after 273 days off for Charlie Johnston — a yard with a reasonable strike rate but this is a significant absence, and early market drift would be a telling sign that connections are not overly confident about the comeback readiness.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Eternal Stakes (Fillies' Listed)

runners_data.name: Assaranca
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has form over 7f in similar Good ground conditions (sim-going: 9/13); P J McDonald rides and she returns just 19 days after her last run, though her recent finishing positions of 6-6 suggest she needs generous pace to land a blow.|
runners_data.comment: Positioned too far off the pace at Epsom last time, Assaranca still shaped with promise in a strong Listed heat, suggesting there is ability to show at this level; effective over 7-8f on any surface. A repeat of her best is needed to figure from stall nine here.

runners_data.name: Classic Cuvee
runners_data.note: R Varian's filly returns after 32 days and has a strong Good-ground 7f profile (1W2P from five runs), but her last three efforts have been modest; hold-up style means she needs a strong pace to close and that may not materialise here.|
runners_data.comment: Blinkers go on for the first time and Classic Cuvee likely found a Listed contest too hot for her last month — comfortably held on form that had previously been better. Effective over 7f on a sound surface, a sharper display is required to land a blow here.

runners_data.name: Confide In Me
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just two starts but won on her most recent outing over this trip; despite being a natural front-runner or prominent racer by style, the depth of pace in this field means she is squeezed out of that position, which is a significant tactical disadvantage on debut at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced after just two recent starts, Confide In Me matched her debut form when runner-up at Redcar last time, yet steps into significantly tougher company now. Acts over today's distance and going, but a major leap forward is needed to threaten at this level.

runners_data.name: Ellusive Butterfly
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone pace-setter with a clear role; her OR of 100 is the highest in the field, she is comfortable on Good ground over 7f, and K R Burke's yard is in solid form — the key question is whether her recent Good-ground form (four of five runs missed a place) holds up when asked to lead at Listed level.|
runners_data.comment: Winning form at Listed level in a 7f heat last time out makes Ellusive Butterfly a real contender here — effective on any going and versatile from 7-8f. Now carries a penalty though, which is the one thing rivals will be hoping tells against her.

runners_data.name: Albaydaa
runners_data.note: W J Haggas sends out a filly with a fine 7f Good-ground record (1W3P from six relevant runs) and Tom Marquand in the saddle; she is naturally a prominent racer but the crowded pace scenario pushes her back from her ideal slot, meaning she must settle for a chasing position that slightly blunts her effectiveness.|
runners_data.comment: Albaydaa has two wins in her last five starts and arrived at this level in excellent heart, taking a handicap here last time with a narrow but decisive display showing real tenacity. Effective from 6-7f on a range of surfaces, she tops our figures and has scope for more at this grade.

runners_data.name: Applesandpears
runners_data.note: E Bethell's filly won twice on standard ground and D Tudhope takes the ride, but her last two runs — 8th and 3rd — have been inconsistent; she wants to race up with the pace, and being displaced from that position by Ellusive Butterfly and Figjam means she races against her grain today.|
runners_data.comment: Placed here at Carlisle last time, which gives Applesandpears a course angle to cling to, and she handles today's distance and going. Our figures rank her ninth of ten, however, and she needs to find considerably more to threaten the market leaders.

runners_data.name: Figjam
runners_data.note: K Scott's representative finished 6th last time but has won over 6f on Good ground and Jason Hart is an aggressive pilot who will press for position early; of the prominent types, Figjam has the profile to actually secure a place behind Ellusive Butterfly rather than being shuffled back.|
runners_data.comment: A competitive sort who fits well at 6f on testing ground and has done enough over today's trip to suggest she belongs at this level; Figjam ran down the field over 7f last time, a flat effort, and the return to her best form is required. The ability is there — consistency is the question.

runners_data.name: Golden Palace
runners_data.note: R A Fahey's filly has shown consistency at 7f on Good ground (sim-going: 6/7 2W3P) and Barry McHugh can be positive from the gate; recent form of 3rd and 7th is moderate, but if she slots in behind the leader she is a genuine player for minor honours.|
runners_data.comment: Close-up third at Musselburgh last time — just two lengths behind the principals — Golden Palace has the class and stamina for today's trip and goes well on a sound surface. Yet to get her head in front in recent starts, but capable of a sharp effort at this grade.

runners_data.name: Just A Girl
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Charlie Johnston who has placed twice over 7f on Good ground recently; Connor Beasley handles her well, but she needs a strong gallop to close from off the pace and a single front-runner scenario on fast ground may leave her without the tow she requires.|
runners_data.comment: Proximity at Carlisle last time — a close second in a 7f handicap here — gives Just A Girl a strong course-and-distance angle, and she handles today's ground. Our figures rank her eighth in this ten-runner field, however, and she requires considerably more to reach the front end.

runners_data.name: Stimulative Trip
runners_data.note: D Menuisier's filly won over this trip on Good ground but hasn't raced for 51 days and her last two efforts (9th, 6th) were disappointing; the layoff combined with those poor runs is a concern, and she needs to recapture her best to be competitive here.|
runners_data.comment: Placed on the clock at Chantilly on her last start, running to level beaten a little over three lengths, Stimulative Trip handles today's distance and going and arrives here with a jockey who knows this course well retained. Two disappointing finishes before that win are the main concern.

races.paceDynamic: Ellusive Butterfly is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressure expected, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the off on Good to Firm ground over 7f at Carlisle. Behind her, Albaydaa, Applesandpears, and Confide In Me are all natural prominent racers who cannot all secure their preferred positions and will be forced wider or further back than ideal, compressing the midfield and creating a bunched chasing pack. Figjam and Golden Palace are the prominent types most likely to actually slot in behind Ellusive Butterfly given their draw and jockey aggression, while the redistributed trio will effectively race in a crowded midfield against their instincts. With a single pace-setter setting a measured tempo on fast ground, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel comfortably in behind the leader and produce a sustained finish — classic prominent-to-midfield profiles who get a clean run home are most advantaged, while pure hold-up horses may find the pace insufficient to pull them through late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ellusive Butterfly Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Ellusive Butterfly gets a clean break and is allowed to roll along at her own tempo without being harassed, setting a fair but manageable pace.
scenarios.body: If Ellusive Butterfly gets a clean break and is allowed to roll along at her own tempo without being harassed, setting a fair but manageable pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Ellusive Butterfly sets a pace that is just fast enough to stretch the hold-up horses but leaves herself vulnerable to a close stalker coming with a well-timed run.
scenarios.body: If Ellusive Butterfly sets a pace that is just fast enough to stretch the hold-up horses but leaves herself vulnerable to a close stalker coming with a well-timed run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected, creating enough of a true gallop that the field spreads and hold-up horses find daylight in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: If the pace is stronger than expected, creating enough of a true gallop that the field spreads and hold-up horses find daylight in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types disrupt the race order early, causing a ragged pace and a sprint finish that plays into stamina doubts.
scenarios.body: If the redistributed prominent types disrupt the race order early, causing a ragged pace and a sprint finish that plays into stamina doubts.

watchPoints.text: Ellusive Butterfly's ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the defining factor — if she idles in front or is pressured unexpectedly by Figjam or Golden Palace in the first half-mile, the entire race dynamic changes.

Albaydaa, Applesandpears, and Confide In Me are all natural prominent types who cannot all get their positions — watch for congestion and interference in the first two furlongs as they jostle behind Ellusive Butterfly.

Classic Cuvee's hold-up style requires a genuine pace to make ground from the rear; if the gallop is modest, Ray Dawson will have no pace to aim at and she may find herself flat-footed in the straight.

Good to Firm ground (confirmed going report) strongly favours horses with proven fast-ground form — Albaydaa (3/6 sim-going wins/places) and Classic Cuvee (1W2P) are the hold-up/prominent types with the clearest Fast-ground credentials.

Stimulative Trip's 51-day absence is the longest in the field — D Menuisier's recent record (2/22 over 14 days) suggests limited confidence, and a return to form off a break would be required to factor.|

races.name: Stablemate By AGMA Carlisle Bell Handicap

runners_data.name: Canvas
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Dixon who has won at this trip on good ground; the 39-day break is not a concern given the trainer's 2/22 14-day strike rate, and sim-going figures show three wins on good; will need a clean run from the rear and daylight in a big field.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Newmarket last time off a mark just 1lb lower than today's, Canvas ran to her level on a sound surface over 8f and is capable of a decent effort here. Our figures place her fifteenth of seventeen, however, and she needs considerably more to reach the frame in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Glenfinnan
runners_data.note: Beasley rides for Dods and this six-year-old returned to form when winning over 8f on good ground last time out (11 days ago); suited by today's conditions but the tongue-tie is noted and the step back from 7f recent runs is a minor query.
runners_data.comment: Carrying a hood for the first time and having been keen and unable to see out the trip last time at the same mark as today, Glenfinnan needs a cleaner race here; still weighted competitively on earlier form and handles soft and good to firm. A big unknown with the new headgear.

runners_data.name: Vixey
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 210 days off for a low-activity trainer; the form figures show she was placed at 8f on good ground and won at 7f on good, making the going and trip fine, but the lengthy absence and 0/2 T14 rate demand caution about peak fitness.
runners_data.comment: Away 210 days — a lengthy absence — and having been far too keen in the early stages last time, Vixey faces a stiff task on her return. Acts over 7f on a sound surface and not soft; our figures rank her last of seventeen and a bounce-back from that effort is essential.

runners_data.name: Naples
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Hollinshead with course-compatible headgear (hood) and placed on good ground at 8f previously; the trainer's 2/10 T14 record is solid and this horse tracks the pace naturally, though a string of softer-ground runs may mean today's good-to-firm is firmer than ideal.
runners_data.comment: First-time cheekpieces and a solid third last time over today's distance and going — Naples is effective from a mile to 10f on heavy and good. Not without a shout in a wide-open field, though our figures have her ranked fifth overall.

runners_data.name: Degale
runners_data.note: Barron runner who is a genuine hold-up horse in terms of natural style but, with multiple closers in this field, will find himself racing further forward than usual; best run at 8f on good ground was a third, and the 8-day turnaround keeps him fresh, but racing out of his preferred position tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Keen and unable to see out the mile at Thirsk eight days ago, Degale has a patchy recent record and is yet to win in her last five starts; acts at 8f on a sound surface. Our figures rank her sixteenth here and a run close to her very best is needed just to figure.

runners_data.name: Enola Grey
runners_data.note: Tutty's six-year-old is naturally a hold-up performer, though the packed rear means she is unlikely to get that position; 117 days off course is a significant query, the sim-going figures on good are weak (0W0P in 3), and the Stalls going preference is absent here — hard to fancy.
runners_data.comment: Off the track for 117 days, Enola Grey returns from a break with the bulk of her better form coming on the AW; she handles today's distance and going but this is turf after a long absence. A return to form is entirely possible with fitness on her side.

runners_data.name: Persuasion
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up horse trained by Barron with an 11-day turnaround; won a 7f race on good ground earlier this season and has course experience, but OR 85 means a penalty in weight and the horse's best form has come over 7f rather than today's mile — stamina is the key question.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time off 86 — 1lb higher than today — Persuasion ran to her level and the switch back to a mile is a genuine positive given her 7f profile; acts on any ground. The main risk is that she has been below her best in recent starts and needs to recapture earlier form.

runners_data.name: Lexington Jet
runners_data.note: Loughnane's four-year-old won at 8f on good ground and has tactical speed that means he can sit closer in a big field than his hold-up tag implies; the blinkers and a 4/23 T14 rate from an in-form yard are positive, and the OR 85 reflects genuine class for this grade.
runners_data.comment: Found wanting over 10f last time when sixth at the top of the weights, Lexington Jet drops to a more suitable trip here and clearly enjoys getting out in front; three wins in his last six on good and AW. Our figures rank him fourteenth, though, and the drop back to preferred conditions is the main selling point.

runners_data.name: Billyb
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, ridden by McDonald who will exploit the clean lead immediately; STYLE_FIT flag is noted as he may be going faster than ideal for his own stamina at the mile trip, and recent form has been modest, but the controlling position in a field of closers makes him genuinely dangerous.
runners_data.comment: Keen and raced off the pace last time at York where she ran down the field, Billyb is usually held up and needs things to unfold more favourably here; effective from 7-10f, acts on a range of surfaces. A clear rebound from that effort is required and she gets first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Altareq
runners_data.note: Goldie's four-year-old is a natural prominent racer with a remarkable record of placing — second or third in four of five 2024 starts — and the Mulrennan booking from a yard firing at 8/47 T14 is significant; handles good-to-firm and the mile trip well, and is ideally suited to track Billyb into the straight.
runners_data.comment: Previously in fine shape with three placings from four starts, Altareq was well below par when well beaten at York most recently — unable to get into the race from off the pace. A top jockey and prior form over a mile on a sound surface give him strong credentials if that run is discounted.

runners_data.name: Priapos
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good ground and placed at the trip on similar terrain, making today's conditions a clean fit for Makin's four-year-old; the hood (hg:p) is a positive, only 25 days since last run, and the horse has the tactical speed from mid-division to make a forward move turning in — a strong each-way profile.
runners_data.comment: Landed a 7-8f handicap at Carlisle last time with authority off a 3lb lower mark, finishing well under pressure — Priapos has two wins in his last five starts and handles any ground. The yard is in good heart and first-time cheekpieces add interest; stepping up 3lb is the only reservation.

runners_data.name: Swift Salian
runners_data.note: Barron's consistent prominent runner has finished second five times in recent starts, including twice at 8f on good ground; the T14 rate of 2/7 is acceptable, the horse is comfortable in its role tracking the pace, and today's conditions suit — finds a way to get beaten but will be close.
runners_data.comment: A pattern of consistent placings in recent outings — placed five times in five starts without adding to her tally — Swift Salian held her level at Nottingham last time off the same mark as today; effective from 8-9f on any surface. A reliable yardstick who needs a slice of luck to get her head in front.

runners_data.name: Leadenhall
runners_data.note: Easterby's six-year-old has won twice over 8f on good ground in recent form and the T14 rate of 8/104 from a high-volume yard is noted; as a genuine hold-up horse redistributed into midfield due to traffic, the three wins at the sim-going mark are encouraging but getting a clear run in a 17-runner field is the obstacle.
runners_data.comment: Leadenhall took two wins from his last five starts, landing a tight finish at Nottingham just four days ago off the same mark here — running keenly but finishing well under a positive ride. A top trainer here at Carlisle, no penalty to carry, and a claiming jockey: the one to beat at the weights.

runners_data.name: Rajapour
runners_data.note: O'Meara runner with a hood and tongue-tie who is a true hold-up performer; has placed at 8f on good ground on multiple occasions (0W3P sim-going) and the 9-day turnaround keeps him sharp, but being pushed into midfield rather than dropping to the rear means his finishing run will be shorter than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Held up and needing pace to target, Rajapour wore too much ground off at Wetherby last time in first-time combined headgear; effective around 8-9f on any going. Our figures rank her thirteenth, and she needs a strong gallop and the gear to spark the improvement required.

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Jardine's six-year-old is at home running from behind but his recent form at much longer distances — 16f, 17f — is a significant concern for a flat-out mile on good-to-firm ground; redistributed into midfield, and with only two places from 15 sim-going runs, the profile does not fit today's race shape.
runners_data.comment: Second at Ayr five days ago off the same mark, Mr Lincoln ran solidly but appeared to find the flat mile insufficient on stamina grounds. Acts on soft and good from up to 13f; yet to win in recent starts but placed form is consistent and he will not be far away.

runners_data.name: Financer
runners_data.note: Easterby's five-year-old carries blinkers and has been placed at 8-10f on good ground, but the 0W3P sim-going record and a string of fourth-place finishes paint a picture of a horse that gets close without winning; mapped into midfield from his natural hold-up position, the blinkers may sharpen him but class appears to be the ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Blinkers on for the first time and a trainer in good form — Financer is a generally consistent type who ran to her level at York last time off a 2lb higher mark than today's; suits 9-10f on any ground. Yet to win in recent starts but rated our second-best horse in the race.

runners_data.name: Be Frank
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' six-year-old has been consistently mid-pack in recent starts at 7-8f and the going figures are fine; redistributed from the rear into midfield, this horse's profile — moderate OR 72, placed occasionally on good ground — does not suggest it can win against stronger rivals, even if the run style suits better from this position.
runners_data.comment: Trainer out of form at 4% strike rate over the last fortnight, and Be Frank has produced five consecutive well-beaten efforts — prominent at Chester last time but never landing a blow, beaten five-and-a-half lengths. Acts over 7f to a mile on a sound surface and has a workable mark if returning to something like her better level.

races.paceDynamic: Billyb is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with P J McDonald aboard, will stride into a clear lead from the outset, setting a measured, uncontested gallop on good-to-firm ground over this flat Carlisle mile. With no genuine challenger for the lead, the pace is likely to be honest but not scorching, meaning Billyb controls tempo and the race will develop as a tactical exercise from halfway. The prominent types — Vixey, Naples, Altareq, and Swift Salian — are best placed to track the leader and are unlikely to allow the race to turn into a dawdle, but equally none of them will force a speed duel. This shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a powerful late finish, except that the field is loaded with true hold-up types: Degale, Enola Grey, Rajapour, Leadenhall, Mr Lincoln, Financer, and Be Frank are all genuine closers who cannot all settle at the rear as they would naturally prefer, meaning the midfield will be congested and truly late closers may find daylight harder to secure — the primary beneficiary profile is prominent racers who track the pace from second or third and have the class to quicken past Billyb in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Billyb's uncontested lead produces a true but not fast pace and the prominent-to-midfield chasers travel sweetly into contention turning for home.
scenarios.body: If Billyb's uncontested lead produces a true but not fast pace and the prominent-to-midfield chasers travel sweetly into contention turning for home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Billyb Dictates And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If McDonald controls the tempo to perfection, the gallop is genuinely steady in the middle stages, and no prominent horse has the gears to close.
scenarios.body: If McDonald controls the tempo to perfection, the gallop is genuinely steady in the middle stages, and no prominent horse has the gears to close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to set up a proper finish and one of the congested midfield runners finds a run at the right moment.
scenarios.body: If the pace is strong enough to set up a proper finish and one of the congested midfield runners finds a run at the right moment.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly quickens early and the prominent horses are dragged into a battle, leaving the race wide open for a late sweep.
scenarios.body: If the pace unexpectedly quickens early and the prominent horses are dragged into a battle, leaving the race wide open for a late sweep.

watchPoints.text: Billyb (McDonald) will stride clear immediately and control all fractions — watch whether McDonald allows a genuine pace or crawls, as a very slow tempo dramatically increases Billyb's winning chance and removes the prominent trackers' ability to quicken past him.

Altareq and Swift Salian are both prominent types racing for the same second or third position behind Billyb — if they race too keenly tracking each other in the early stages, both may empty in the final furlong, opening the door for a midfield horse to come through.

The redistribution of seven genuine hold-up horses into midfield creates a wide, congested middle pack — watch for traffic problems on the turn into the straight, particularly for Priapos and Lexington Jet, who need a clean run to produce their finish.

Vixey's 210-day layoff makes her fitness a live concern despite the prominent style that suits the race shape — if she shows any sign of blowing hard early or dropping out tamely, it confirms she needed the run and the race shape analysis should discount her.

Carlisle is reported good-to-firm for this race despite the declared going of Good — that faster surface marginally favours horses with clean action and proven good-to-firm form, and Canvas (3W4P sim-going) and Leadenhall (3W4P sim-going) both have strong records in these conditions worth monitoring.

races.name: Stablemate By AGMA Cumberland Plate Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Wanderlust
runners_data.note: Unresolved in terms of running style with a U tag; Tom Marquand's booking lends tactical flexibility, and she has course-going form on similar ground, but her last five runs show a consistent inability to win — three recent fourths and a fifth suggest she hits a flat spot late and rarely finds enough.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Newbury last time at what looks about British level suggests Wanderlust needs more to compete here, and she is already ranked sixth on our figures. A trainer in good form and proven stamina from 10-12f on soft and good are genuine points in her favour.

runners_data.name: Wine Dark Sea
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's four-year-old has winning form at 1m2f on Good and Stamina handicap tracks, and the style-fit flag (0.91) indicates she is operating out of her most natural role as a prominent runner; Lewis Edmunds can carve out an easy lead, but the real question is whether she stays strongly enough over 1m3f after 46 days off.|
runners_data.comment: Sharp form at Ascot last time when landing a handicap with something to spare off a lower mark makes Wine Dark Sea among the stronger claims in this field; effective over 12f on good ground and the AW. The step up to a competitive Class 4 off a higher mark is the one caveat.

runners_data.name: Secret Beach
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent type with two wins and six places in similar going across 12 furlongs for David McCain; headgear (t) suggests a tendency to switch off focus, and after 47 days off, sharpness is a mild query — but her Good ground record (2W6P in 15 sim-going runs) gives meaningful confidence she handles conditions.|
runners_data.comment: Held to her level at Chester last time — fifth over 12f on a sound surface — Secret Beach arrives here in first-time headgear and handles today's trip. Our ratings place her tenth of twelve, however, and she needs to step up markedly to be a factor.

runners_data.name: Golden West
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up five-year-old holds a reasonable Good-ground record across an honest sample but has been out-of-form recently (4-8-7-8-4 in last five); only 11 days since last run is positive in terms of fitness, yet his trip profile skews shorter than today's 1m3f and this distance is a stretch.|
runners_data.comment: Came home well from off the pace at Chester most recently, finishing not far behind the principals, though without a win in her last five starts Golden West has questions to answer. A top trainer provides a yard angle here at Carlisle and she stays 8-10f.

runners_data.name: Ludo's Landing
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's six-year-old drops to 1m3f from recent runs at 1m4f-1m6f, and his most recent start was a win at 1m2f on Good, making this trip a comfortable middle-ground; blinkers noted, Jason Hart rides, and 28 days since last run is fine — he is suited by today's conditions but needs a proper pace to close into.|
runners_data.comment: Third at Hamilton last time off a mark just a pound higher than today's, Ludo's Landing goes in first-time blinkers and acts over today's trip and going; a trip range of 10-13f makes today's stamina test manageable. The new headgear means there is an unknown element.

runners_data.name: Trojan Sun
runners_data.note: Won over 1m6f on Good 14 days ago for Jim Goldie, so is fit and in form; Paul Mulrennan will look to adopt a prominent position from stall, and the drop back to 1m3f may suit if he can travel more freely — three Good-ground wins from eight similar-going runs underline his affinity for today's surface.|
runners_data.comment: Winning at Carlisle last time with a willing display off a 5lb lower mark — and with a jockey who has an excellent record at this track back aboard — gives Trojan Sun obvious claims despite a penalty. Acts on any turf ground over a mile and beyond; first-time cheekpieces the variable, and the higher weight is the concern.

runners_data.name: Inappropriate
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up stayer — last three runs were over 1m7f — who drops dramatically in trip to 1m3f today, and 120 days off (40 days since a jockey change) adds serious fitness doubt; tongue-strap and cheekpieces in use, and a thin trainer strike rate (0/5 in 14 days) compounds the concern about readiness.|
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces appear for the first time and Inappropriate steps back onto the flat after a handicap hurdle run where she was comfortably held — unable to extend what had been a brief revival. Suits 10f on any ground, but the inconsistency remains the central issue here.

runners_data.name: Austrian Theory
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old is a true hold-up horse by nature, but the field is stacked with closers and he has been redistributed to a midfield mapping; his last ten runs in similar going show zero wins and only two places, and his recent form string of 3-5-9-7-5 offers little to recommend even if he gains his preferred position.|
runners_data.comment: The trainer has a solid record in this race and Austrian Theory tries cheekpieces after a six-length defeat at York last time where she finished strongest in the final furlong; effective over 8-10f on any ground. Yet to win in recent starts, and a significant rebound from that York effort is needed.

runners_data.name: Eroico
runners_data.note: Mark Todhunter's four-year-old comes here having been placed in five of his seven similar-going starts without ever winning; he is a natural hold-up horse bumped forward on the map because of rear congestion, and his style-fit flag (0.90) reflects the likelihood he won't get his true race — his zero wins in fifteen comparable runs demands significant caution.|
runners_data.comment: A long way back at Thirsk last time when tried in a hood and found wanting over the trip — Eroico is our bottom-rated runner here and yet to win in her last five starts. Stays around a mile to 12f and acts on soft and good, but needs everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Dunkeld Dreamer
runners_data.note: Karl Burke's three-year-old is the in-form angle in this race — four wins from nine Good-ground runs and a win just 11 days ago over 1m2f at Goodwood suggests peak fitness; Connor Lee claiming 5lbs is helpful on the weights, and a prominent style on fast ground over today's trip looks ideal — recent form string 514241 conceals a horse who fires fresh.|
runners_data.comment: Finishing strongly at York last time, Dunkeld Dreamer took a tight affair off a 2lb lower mark and has won two of his last six — acts on any going from 7-10f. A live chance off only a modest rise, the main risk being whether recent form is strong enough to hold up at this level.

runners_data.name: Alpine Sierra
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's eight-year-old has won three of his last six including back-to-back wins at 1m1f and 1m2f on Good ground; Lauren Young (claiming jockey) keeps the weight low, and four wins from fifteen similar-going starts suggests he handles conditions reliably — prominent style and in-form profile make him dangerous at a competitive OR of 66.|
runners_data.comment: Three wins in her last six — including a comfortable Carlisle success last time off a lower mark — give Alpine Sierra an eye-catching profile, and she is effective from 7-12f on soft, good and the AW. Our figures rank her well down the field, suggesting she faces a stiff task at the weights.

runners_data.name: Gaelic Approach
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old has a superb recent record — two wins and four places from six similar-going runs — and connections have a strong 14-day strike rate; hold-up style suits the scenario only if a strong pace develops, but his form over 1m2f-1m4f on Good ground (2W4P from 8 runs) suggests the trip and going are squarely in his favour.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent record of two wins in his last five starts, a sound third last time off the same mark as today, and proven over today's distance and going — Gaelic Approach goes in from the foot of the weights and a drop in trip should suit. Our top-rated horse here by some margin.

races.paceDynamic: Wine Dark Sea is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 12-runner field and, with no genuine rival looking to press from the gates, Lewis Edmunds can dictate a comfortable, sustainable gallop through the opening furlongs of this 1m3f trip on Good to Firm ground. Trojan Sun and Secret Beach will likely press forward into prominent positions alongside Dunkeld Dreamer and Alpine Sierra, creating a competitive mid-to-front group but without the aggressive head-to-head pressure that would fragment the pace. Austrian Theory and Eroico are genuine hold-up horses by nature but are redistributed to a midfield mapping because the field's rear is already crowded with hold-up types — Ludo's Landing, Inappropriate, Golden West, and Gaelic Approach all prefer to come from off the pace, meaning the back of the field will be congested and those horses will be racing closer than ideal. With a controlled, unchallenged lead likely set by Wine Dark Sea and a genuinely deep hold-up contingent stuck wide or blocked, this race shape most strongly favours prominent racers who can travel in the first three or four without over-exerting — horses like Dunkeld Dreamer and Alpine Sierra, who can sit handily and produce a sustained finish on fast ground, are ideally suited to what this pace map projects.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Wine Dark Sea dictates an unchallenged, even tempo and the prominent racers behind settle without fighting for position.
scenarios.body: If Wine Dark Sea dictates an unchallenged, even tempo and the prominent racers behind settle without fighting for position.

scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Breaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough for the deep hold-up brigade to close ground through the final three furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough for the deep hold-up brigade to close ground through the final three furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Wins All
scenarios.trigger: If Wine Dark Sea bowls along completely unchallenged and the hold-up group simply cannot reel in the leader over 1m3f.
scenarios.body: If Wine Dark Sea bowls along completely unchallenged and the hold-up group simply cannot reel in the leader over 1m3f.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Fractures, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners contest the early lead aggressively and the field fragments, leaving fatigued leaders vulnerable.
scenarios.body: If multiple prominent runners contest the early lead aggressively and the field fragments, leaving fatigued leaders vulnerable.

watchPoints.text: Alpine Sierra and Dunkeld Dreamer are both in-form prominent types with multiple recent wins on similar going — if either gets a clean prominent position, they are the biggest threat to dominate the race shape that best suits today's likely tempo.

The rear of the field is congested with hold-up types — Gaelic Approach, Ludo's Landing, Golden West, Inappropriate, Austrian Theory, and Eroico all prefer to come from off the pace; watch for traffic issues and blocked runs turning into the straight, particularly for Gaelic Approach who has the best recent form among them.

Wine Dark Sea has a style-fit flag (0.91) and is racing out of role as a lone front-runner — if she fades rapidly in the straight, she could cause interference as the prominent group arrives, creating a chaotic finish in the final furlong.

Trojan Sun won 14 days ago over 1m6f and drops in trip — watch whether Paul Mulrennan elects to press Wine Dark Sea early; if he does, it transforms the pace map from a controlled lead scenario into a contested pace with significant implications for the hold-up horses.

Inappropriate is 120 days since last run with a jockey change flagged and drops sharply in trip from 1m7f — if showing any signs of ring-rustiness in the parade ring or early on, her chance of getting competitive from a hold-up position is minimal.

races.name: Racing Staff Week Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Rogue Attraction
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up filly whose last win came over 6f on Good ground, but she steps up to 7f here for the first time after 236 days off — Bethell's T14 form (3/14) is solid, the p headgear suggests she needs covering up, and she will need the pace to truly collapse for her late run to reach a front-running winner.
runners_data.comment: Away 236 days and in need of a significant return to form having been well beaten in a Listed event last time on unsuitable ground — Rogue Attraction is effective at 6f and gets first-time cheekpieces. Ranked fifth of six, there is ability here but everything needs to click.

runners_data.name: Shushu
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner with two runs, both over 7f at this exact course on Soft, winning the most recent; Varian's T14 is modest (2/27) but Dawson is booked, the horse is race-ready off 14 days, and uncontested control on Good to Firm over a flat 7f is a significant tactical advantage she holds over every rival in this field.
runners_data.comment: Getting off the mark at Yarmouth last time in a clear-cut manner — taking a step forward and showing the right attitude — Shushu now tries handicap company for the first time on today's going; effective at 7f on soft and good to soft. Strong handler and further improvement from this mark looks achievable.

runners_data.name: Mostar Dreams
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a win over 8f on Standard but a turbulent form profile; 138 days off-track is a major flag, the 142lb top weight is punishing in a small-field handicap, and while Keatley's yard is ticking (2/9 T14) the step back to 7f and faster going asks questions her recent starts haven't answered.
runners_data.comment: Prior form before that nightmare outing at Newcastle is genuinely decent — Mostar Dreams has won and shown ability at her best across a wide trip range including today's going. Returning from a break and needing to settle after pulling hard last time; if she does, she could be a real danger.

runners_data.name: Donna Nook
runners_data.note: Strong form over 8f on Good ground — three recent placed efforts at that trip — but drops to 7f here on faster conditions, and her natural preference for a longer hold-up race is compromised by the redistribution forced on her by a rear-loaded field; the tv headgear and Tudhope's experience help, yet the distance and style mismatch temper her chance.
runners_data.comment: Taking to a new headgear combination at Ripon last time, Donna Nook took a tight handicap in a driving finish off a 3lb lower mark — effective from 8-10f on a sound surface. Now 3lb higher but showed enough to suggest she has the class to meet that rise.

runners_data.name: Nanoscience
runners_data.note: Prominent-style three-year-old with a sharp recent record at 7f on Good and Good to Firm (1-3-1-3 in relevant conditions); McDonald's booking is significant, she is the only runner naturally placed to track Shushu into the race, and her style fits the dominant shape better than any other hold-up rival.
runners_data.comment: Two wins from five recent starts, including a narrow but decisive handicap success at Wetherby last time off a 1lb lower mark — Nanoscience showed a willing attitude and acts over today's distance on a sound surface. Our top-rated runner here by a clear margin, she is progressive and more can be expected.

runners_data.name: Who Wants Me
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type, like Donna Nook pushed forward on the map because true hold-up space is scarce; the t headgear suggests she needs settling, 38 days off, zero wins from 15 similar-going starts and the lowest OR in the field (65) all combine to make her the least likely to benefit from any race shape that emerges here.
runners_data.comment: Off 38 days and yet to win in her last five starts, Who Wants Me showed adequate form when held off the pace at Hamilton despite a slow start; suits 7f on soft and good. First-time tongue-tie adds a variable, but our figures rank her joint-last here — an unlikely threat without a jump in form.

races.paceDynamic: Shushu is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, with no natural challenger for the lead, will dictate on a completely uncontested basis over Carlisle's flat 7f on Good to Firm ground. The pace she sets is likely to be measured and controlled — Ray Dawson can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits, and a horse who has already won over this exact course and distance combination in soft ground is not going to be troubled for the early initiative. Nanoscience is the only prominent-style runner and will likely track Shushu in second, while Donna Nook and Who Wants Me — both natural hold-up types — have been redistributed into the midfield on the map simply because the rear is already crowded; neither is genuinely suited to racing prominently, so the horse-for-course front-running dynamic remains clean. This race shape strongly favours either the front-runner herself or a horse with the tactical pace to sit within two lengths of a controlled, uncontested lead and quicken from a prime position when asked — prominent and close-tracking profiles are at a significant premium.

scenarios.title: Shushu Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Shushu leads without any early pressure and dictates a sustainable, honest pace from the front.
scenarios.body: If Shushu leads without any early pressure and dictates a sustainable, honest pace from the front.

scenarios.trigger: If Nanoscience sits a length off Shushu, the pace proves slightly too steady, and McDonald produces a well-timed challenge inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Nanoscience sits a length off Shushu, the pace proves slightly too steady, and McDonald produces a well-timed challenge inside the final furlong.

scenarios.title: Closers Rattle Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If Shushu sets a genuinely strong early gallop that strings the field out and leaves the door ajar for a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: If Shushu sets a genuinely strong early gallop that strings the field out and leaves the door ajar for a sustained late run.

scenarios.title: Mostar Dreams Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Mostar Dreams, who has a course-winning profile and bounces back from a 138-day absence, lands a surprise late challenge.
scenarios.body: If Mostar Dreams, who has a course-winning profile and bounces back from a 138-day absence, lands a surprise late challenge.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Nanoscience (McDonald) sits aggressively on Shushu's quarters from the break — if she does, she turns this into a two-horse match and becomes the biggest danger to the front-runner.

Rogue Attraction returns from 236 days off and wears a hood (p headgear) — monitor her behaviour in the stalls and early behaviour on track, as a sluggish break from this layoff would make her already-difficult hold-up task virtually impossible over 7f.

Donna Nook is a genuine 8f performer on Good ground forced down to 7f on faster conditions while also racing out of her natural hold-up style — if she looks laboured early rather than settled and travelling, write off any chance of her landing a blow.

Mostar Dreams carries 142lbs — the heaviest weight in the race — and returns from 138 days off; watch how she moves to post and whether she gives any visual sign of being ready, as her form is capable of either a big run or a complete no-show.
